clue.text: Scream, seeing mass of debris on church

parts.note: scree is the mass of loose broken rock that collects on a mountain slope

explanation.surface: Someone shrieks at the sight of a heap of rubble piled on a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrill, piercing cry is both a scream and a screech, so the two are synonyms.

parts.note: CL is 150 in Roman numerals (C = 100, L = 50)
AD (anno Domini) labels the present era, the years we live in now

explanation.surface: A number of things, 150 of them, are covered nowadays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is a link word joining the wordplay to the definition 'covered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clad is an old past participle of clothe, so something clad is dressed or covered.

clue.text: There is no lack of interest in his business!

definitions.text: There is no lack of interest in his business!

parts.words: There is no lack of interest in his business!
parts.note: reads like praise for a man whose work fascinates people, but the interest meant is the money charged on loans, which this lender charges at high rates

explanation.surface: A remark that some man's line of work is never dull.
explanation.definitionFit: A moneylender charging excessive rates makes his whole living from interest on loans.

indicators.note: off says the preceding words are spoiled or disordered, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone's man was discouraged from playing the drum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put off' reads as one phrase meaning deterred, but 'put' is part of the fodder and 'off' alone signals the anagram of MY MAN PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The tympanum is the eardrum, and the word is also used of a kettledrum in older writing.

parts.note: explosive suggests fireworks or bombs, but the joke is the sound of a cork or balloon bursting, a pop, attached to a musical show

explanation.surface: A thrilling or dangerous show.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance of popular music is a show built on pop, the word for a small explosion.

clue.text: Illness meant game did not start on Sunday

indicators.note: a game that did not start has lost its opening letter

parts.note: cricket is the bat-and-ball game

explanation.surface: A sickness meant that a Sunday match was called off before it began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meant' is a link word. 'did not start' removes the first letter C from CRICKET, leaving RICKET.
explanation.definitionFit: Rickets is a childhood disease of softened bones caused by lack of vitamin D, so it is an illness.

parts.note: suggests a broadcaster's complaints officer, but the viewers are the eyes and the complaints are eye disorders

explanation.surface: A television company's officer who handles letters from unhappy viewers.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye doctor treats disorders of sight, the ailments of the organs we view with.

indicators.note: a version is a different rendering, so the letters of in corby appear in a new order

explanation.surface: A poem's rendering found in the town of Corby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version' signals rearranging the seven letters of IN CORBY. Corby is a town in Northamptonshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Byronic means in the style of the poet Lord Byron, so broadly poetical and romantic in manner.

clue.text: Rind and potato skin on coat

parts.note: a rind is a hard outer covering, as a shell is
a jacket potato is one baked in its skin, so the skin is its jacket

explanation.surface: Peelings of fruit and potato are dumped on someone's coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' and 'on' are link words joining the two pieces and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A shell jacket is a short tight military jacket worn in undress uniform, a kind of coat.

parts.note: a conductor is one who leads, a leader, and the 's gives the possessive S
the hip is the joint between the thigh and the pelvis

explanation.surface: A conductor's aching joint is said to be key to directing an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Leadership is the capacity to direct and steer other people.

clue.text: Food eaters cannot have, they say

definitions.text: Food eaters cannot have, they say

parts.words: Food eaters cannot have, they say
parts.note: points to the proverb that you cannot have this treat and eat it too, so whoever eats it no longer has it

explanation.surface: A forbidden dish that diners are told they may not order.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says you cannot both keep this sweet baked treat and consume it.

clue.text: Short attempt in various places that are regal

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the jumbled letters of the other
various suggests a mixture, so the letters of places are rearranged
short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: an attempt is a try

explanation.surface: A brief effort made at assorted royal sites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges the letters of places as SCEPAL, and 'that are' is only a link; 'places' looks like locations but is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Sceptral describes the sceptre, the rod a monarch carries, so it means royal.

parts.note: pruning is cutting back branches or stems
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A gardener's favourite proverb, said with a sharp edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the tool: a saw for cutting branches that a gardener uses.
explanation.definitionFit: A pruning saw is a small saw gardeners use to cut back branches of trees and shrubs.

parts.note: looks like a mark in an exam or a round of golf, but a score is twenty, and twenty added to seventy gives the figure

explanation.surface: A test result of better than seventy per cent.
explanation.definitionFit: Twenty more than seventy is the number nine tens, which a score above seventy reaches.

clue.text: One getting ahead out of line

definitions.text: One getting ahead out of line

parts.words: One getting ahead out of line
parts.note: sounds like a rule-breaking careerist, but literally describes someone moving forward out of turn in a line of waiting people

explanation.surface: An ambitious person who gets on by misbehaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who pushes in ahead of others waiting in a line gets ahead improperly.

parts.note: read as hard-ly, with difficulty, that is not with ease, the opposite of a word meaning effortlessly

explanation.surface: A one-word sceptical reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardly' usually means scarcely; here it is taken literally as 'in a hard way', not with ease.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with difficulty is the reverse of doing it with comfort, the literal sense of the answer split as un-easily.

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about
VI is six in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: Roughly half a dozen are eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviare, an older spelling of caviar, is the salted roe of sturgeon, fish eggs.

parts.note: sounds like asking what case an étui is in, but an étui is itself a small case, and the old name for such a case is the word for the plucking tool it held

explanation.surface: A puzzle about a small ornamental case.
explanation.walkthrough: An étui is a small decorative case for needles or toiletries; in older English such a case was called a tweezer-case or simply a tweezer.
explanation.definitionFit: An old English name for a small étui-like case of instruments was this word, from the plucking tool kept inside.

clue.text: Lady I name during test on the way back

indicators.note: during places the following pieces within the reversed word
on the way back means the word for test is read in reverse

parts.note: an exam is a test

explanation.surface: A woman called I mid-test as she was returning home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the way back' turns EXAM into MAXE, and 'during' puts I and N inside it: MAX-IN-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Maxine is a woman's first name, so it names a lady.

parts.note: Inverness is a Scottish town and also a sleeveless cloak, a cape, so a town that is a cape suits a South African city

explanation.surface: A Scottish Highland town wrongly placed in the far south of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: An Inverness cape is a man's cloak, and Inverness is a town; the South African city's name is cape plus town.
explanation.definitionFit: The major South African port city's name splits into a cloak word and a settlement word, both of which Inverness can be.

parts.note: Pat (Patrick) is the stock name for an Irishman in crosswords
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Irish actor appearing in a movie.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a thin coating or sheen on a surface, a film of oxidation or age.

clue.text: The sash removed from the smashing vase

indicators.note: removed from says the letters of one word are taken out of the other

explanation.surface: Someone takes the sash off a stunning vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'removed from' takes S, A, S, H out of SMASHING in order, leaving M, I, N, G.
explanation.definitionFit: Ming porcelain, from China's Ming dynasty, is famous for its precious vases.

parts.note: seems to mean slides and charts in a presentation, but means a pair of lenses worn to help sight

explanation.surface: Charts and slides used in teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeglasses aid vision, and impressive shows are visual too, so both senses fit.

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, and the 's gives a further S

explanation.surface: A policeman's next swear word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' suggests a policeman, but it is the metal, whose chemical symbol is Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: A cuss is a curse, an oath or swear word uttered in anger.

clue.text: Brittle and crumbly, can be cooked quickly, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the words before are spoken, and we take their sound

parts.note: something that can be cooked quickly in a pan is able to be fried, fry-able

explanation.surface: Food that falls apart easily is said to be quick to fry.
explanation.definitionFit: Friable describes material that breaks up into small pieces easily, such as soil or old plaster.

parts.note: single means one
a stage in a process is a step

explanation.surface: A single phase of a ballroom routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is a link word here joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The one-step is a ballroom dance of the early twentieth century in quick march time.
